Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:1.english: He splits [it] open - [This means] he tears [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:2.hebrew: בנסכא - שהן חתיכות ארוכות, וכל זמן שמקצתן בפנים, לא קנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:2.english: With a metal bar - For they are long pieces, and as long as part of them is inside [the private domain], he has not acquired [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:3.english: And we ask: "And since there are laces" - Straps that are called estoldz [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:4.hebrew: מפיק ליה עד פומיה ושקיל - וכיון דמצי למשקלינהו, קני. ולענין שבת לא מיחייב עד דמפיק להו לשנצין, דעל ידו הוא אגוד לרה"י, שהרי לא יצאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:4.english: He carries it out as far as its mouth and takes [the contents] - And since he is able to take them, he acquires [them]. However, regarding Shabbat, he is not liable until he carries out the laces, since through them [the purse] is [still] tied to the private domain, for they have not gone out.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:1:5.english: And they are wound around it - For he cannot take it out without [the] laces.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:2:1.english: Abaye assumed the opinion [of Rava], etc. - Both of them retracted their statements and switched them.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:3:1.hebrew: ביד חייב - משיצאו הפירות, ואע"פ שגופו ברשות היחיד, ולא אמרינן אגד גופו שמיה אגד:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:3:1.english: In [his] hand, he is liable - Once the fruit has gone out [into the public domain], even though his body is in the private domain, and we do not say [that] the connection of his body is considered a connection.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:3:2.english: In a vessel, he is exempt - As long as part of the vessel is in his house.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:3:3.hebrew: ביד פטור - דאגד גופו שמיה אגד, דידו בתר גופו גרירא. בכלי חייב, וקשיא אתרוייהו למה שהחליפו שיטתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:3:3.english: In [his] hand, he is exempt - For the attachment of his body is considered an attachment, since his hand is drawn after his body. [If he carried them out] in a vessel, he is liable. And there is a difficulty regarding both of them [as to] why they reversed their positions.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:4:1.hebrew: התם למעלה מג' - וטעמא משום דלא נח, ולא משום אגד גופה:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:4:1.english: There, above three [handbreadths] - And the reason [he is exempt] is because it did not come to rest, and not because of [the hand's] connection to the body.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:4:2.hebrew: והכא למטה מג' - דליכא למיפטרי' משום הנחה, דכמונח דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:4:2.english: And here, below three [handbreadths] - For one cannot exempt him on account of [a lack of] placing [it down], since it is considered as if placed [on the ground].

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:5:1.hebrew: שכן משא בני קהת - "בכתף ישאו" (במדבר ז׳:ט׳), וימין ושמאל וחיק אורח ארעא. ובשם רבינו יצחק בר יהודה מצאתי, שאמר בשם רב האי, שמפורש בהש"ס ירושלמי: "ופקודת אלעזר בן אהרן הכהן שמן המאור וקטורת הסמים ומנחת התמיד ושמן המשחה" — [שמן] אחד בימין, [ושמן] אחד בשמאל, והקטורת בחיקו, והחביתין בכתף:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:5:1.english: As [this was] the carrying of the sons of Kehat - "On the shoulder they shall carry" (Numbers 7:9), and [carrying in the] right [hand], left [hand], or lap is the normal manner. And in the name of Rabbeinu Yitzchak bar Yehudah I found that he said in the name of Rav Hai that it is explicitly stated in the Jerusalem Talmud: "And the charge of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest: the oil for lighting, and the fragrant incense, and the daily meal-offering, and the anointing oil" — one [oil] in the right [hand], and one [oil] in the left [hand], and the incense in his lap, and the chavitin [daily meal-offering] on the shoulder.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:5:4.hebrew: ופיה למטה - אין דרך הוצאה בכך, אבל פיה למעלה דרך הוצאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:5:4.english: And its opening downward - This is not a [normal] manner of carrying out, whereas [with] its opening upward, [it is a normal] manner of carrying out.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:5:5.english: The hem of his cloak - The lower edge.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:6:1.hebrew: המוציא משאוי למעלה מי' - מעבירו באויר בידו ואינו על כתפו, וגבוה מן הארץ [עשרה] קאמר, דאי במונח על כתפו, מתניתין היא. והא דתנן (לקמן שבת דף ק.): הזורק ד' אמות בכותל למעלה מעשרה כזורק באויר, אלמא אין למעלה מעשרה רשות הרבים — דווקא זורק, אבל מעביר חייב, דיליף מבני קהת במשכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:6:1.english: One who carries out a load above ten [handbreadths] - [This means] he carries it through the air in his hand and it is not on his shoulder, and he is speaking of [when it is] ten [handbreadths] above the ground, for if [he meant] when it is resting on his shoulder, that is [already taught in] our Mishnah. And as for that which we learned in a Mishnah (below, Shabbat 100a): "One who throws [an object] four cubits onto a wall above ten [handbreadths] is like one who throws in the air," thus [proving that] above ten [handbreadths] is not a public domain — [that applies] specifically to one who throws, but one who carries [it] is liable, since it is derived from the sons of Kehat in the Tabernacle.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:6:2.english: Which is by the Tabernacle, etc. - [The verse] speaks of the hangings of the courtyard.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:6:3.hebrew: אף מזבח - גובהו י' אמות, והוצרך לסובבו בקלעים של י' אמות רחב. ומה אני מקיים וג' אמות קומתו (שמות כ״ז:א׳)? משפת סובב ולמעלה. ומה אני מקיים וקומה ה' דקלעים? משפת מזבח ולמעלה. כך מפורש בזבחים (דף נט:), שהיו הקלעים ט"ו אמות:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:6:3.english: So too, [the] altar - Its height was ten cubits, and it was necessary to surround it with hangings of ten cubits in width [i.e., height]. And how do I uphold [the verse], "and three cubits its height" (Exodus 27:1)? [It refers to the height] from the edge of the surrounding ledge and upward. And how do I uphold [the verse], "and the height [was] five [cubits]" regarding the hangings? [It refers to the height] from the edge of the altar and upward. Thus is it explained in Zevachim (59b), that the hangings were fifteen cubits [high].

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:7:1.hebrew: מכאן אתה למד - דקס"ד שאר הלוים נמי גביהי כמשה:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:7:1.english: From here you derive - For [the Gemara] assumes that the other Levites were also as tall as Moses.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:7:2.hebrew: תלתא מלעיל - וכיון דמזבח י' אמות והוא נושא בכתף, כדכתיב (במדבר ז׳:ט׳) ״ולבני קהת לא נתן (עגלות) וגו'״, והלוים י' אמות — כי מדלו ליה תילתא למעלה מראשיהן או מכתיפו, נמצא גבוה מן הארץ קרוב לשליש של י' אמות, דהוו טובא טפי, יותר מי' טפחים:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:7:2.english: One-third above - And since the altar [is] ten cubits [tall], and it is carried on the shoulder — as it is written (Numbers 7:9): "But to the sons of Kohath he did not give [wagons], etc." — and the Levites [are] ten cubits [tall], when they lift one-third of it above their heads or [above] their shoulders, it is found [to be] high above the ground [by] close to a third of ten cubits, which is much more, more than ten handbreadths.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - לא גביהי לוים, ולאו ממזבח גמרינן, דשמא לוים לא גביהי אלא ז' אמות, ואין משאן דמזבח גבוה מן הארץ אלא ב' או ג' טפחים. ומארון גמר לה ר' אלעזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:1.english: And if you wish, say - The Levites were not [that] tall, and we do not derive [it] from the altar, for perhaps the Levites were only seven cubits tall, and their burden of the altar was only two or three handbreadths above the ground. And Rabbi Elazar derived it from the Ark.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:2.hebrew: אשתכח דלמעלה מי' קאי - טובא. אפילו אין גובהן של לוים אלא ג' אמות כמונו, הרי י"ח טפחים, וארון אינו תלוי למטה מכתפותיהן אלא ו' טפחים וב' שלישי טפח, אישתכח דגבוה י' ויותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:2.english: It is found that it stood above ten [handbreadths] - [By] a great deal. Even if the height of the Levites is only three cubits like us, behold, [that is] eighteen handbreadths, and the Ark hangs below their shoulders only six handbreadths and two-thirds of a handbreadth; [thus] it is found that it is ten [handbreadths] high and more.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:3.hebrew: וליגמר ממשה - שפרש המשכן, ונמצא דגובהן של לוים עשר אמות, ונילף מלוים נושאי המזבח:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:3.english: And let us derive [it] from Moses - Who spread [the curtains of] the Tabernacle, and [thus] it is found that the height of the Levites was ten cubits, and let us derive [the law] from the Levites who carried the altar.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:8:4.english: As the Master said - In Tractate Nedarim.

Rashi on Shabbat 92a:9:1.hebrew: אנשי הוצל - היו נושאין כדי מים ויין על ראשיהן, ואין אוחזין אותם בידים:
Rashi on Shabbat 92a:9:1.english: The people of Hotzal - They would carry jugs of water and wine on their heads, and would not hold them with [their] hands.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:1:1.hebrew: דאי בעי מפקע ליה - נראה לר"י שכיסין שלהם לא היו תפורות בחוזק כמו שלנו, ולהכי פריך ממקום התפירה ולא ממקום אחר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:1:1.english: For if he wishes, he can tear it - It appears to the Ri that their purses were not sewn as strongly as ours, and therefore [the Gemara] asks from the place of the sewing and not from another place.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:2:1.english: And a contradiction is raised between Abaye and Abaye - The Gemara knew with certainty that this statement that it cites was said after they retracted [their positions]:

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:3:1.hebrew: המוציא בפיו כו' - והא דתנן באמרו לו (כריתות ד' יג:): "אם היתה שבת והוציאו בפיו — חייב", ה"מ אוכלים שדרכן להוציאן בפיו בשעת אכילה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:3:1.english: One who carries out in his mouth, etc. - And [as for] that which we learned in the Mishnah in [Chapter] Amru Lo (Keritot 13b): "If it was Shabbat and he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable" — that applies [specifically] to foods, which it is normal to carry out in one's mouth at the time of eating.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:4:1.hebrew: התם למעלה מג' - ונהי דלאו שמיה אגד, הנחה ליכא כדפירש בקונטרס. הקשה ה"ר אלחנן: לרבה, דמוקי מתני' בריש מכילתין (דף ד.) כר"ע, דאמר קלוטה כמי שהונחה דמיא — בהך בבא דמייתי הכא, אמאי שניהם פטורין? והלא למעלה מג' לר' עקיבא כמו למטה מג' לרבנן? וי"ל: דרבה סבר אגד גוף שמיה אגד. ור"י מפרש: התם למעלה מג' — ואית לן למימר דשמיה אגד, כדאמר בפ"ק (דף ג.) דידו בתר גופו גריר; הכא למטה מג' — דלאו שמיה אגד:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:4:1.english: "There, [it is] above three [handbreadths]" - And even though it is not considered an attachment [to the body], there is no placing down [of the object], as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres. Rabbi Elchanan raised a difficulty: According to Rabbah, who establishes the Mishnah at the beginning of our tractate (4a) in accordance with Rabbi Akiva — who says that an object suspended in the air is considered as if it has been placed down — in this clause that [the Gemara] cites here, why are both of them exempt? Is not [the airspace] above three [handbreadths] according to Rabbi Akiva like [that] below three [handbreadths] according to the Rabbis? And one can answer that Rabbah holds that attachment to the body is considered an attachment. And the Ri explains: "There, [it is] above three [handbreadths]" — and we must say that it is considered an attachment [to his body], as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter (3a) that his hand is drawn after his body; "Here, [it is] below three [handbreadths]" — for it is not considered an attachment [to his body].

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:5:1.hebrew: לאחר ידו ברגלו - ולספרים דגרס כלאחר ידו, י"ל דברגלו הוי פירוש כלאחר ידו; ומיהו גירסא קמא ניחא טפי, דהכי תניא בברייתא בגמרא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:5:1.english: Le'achar yado [behind his hand], with his foot - And according to the texts that read ke-le'achar yado [in a backhanded manner], one can say that "with his foot" is an explanation of ke-le'achar yado; however, the first reading is more satisfactory, for so it is taught in a baraita in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:5:2.hebrew: במרפקו - הוא שקורין קוד"א, ולא כמו שפירש בקונטרס אישיל"ש, מדתנן באהלות (פ"א מ"ח): "רמ"ח אברים באדם — שלשים בפיסת היד, ו' בכל אצבע, שנים בקנה, שנים במרפק, אחד בזרוע, שנים בכתף כו'", משמע דמרפק הוא למטה מן הזרוע. וכן בפרק האומר משקלי (ערכין יט:): ידי ורגלי עלי — ממלא חבית מים, ומכניס ביד עד העציל וברגל עד הארכובה, ולעציל קרי ליה במתניתין דהתם במרפקו; ותרגום של "אצילי ידי" — "מרפקי ידיה" (יחזקאל י״ג:י״ח), משמע דעציל היינו קוד"א, שהוא ביד כנגד ארכובה ברגל. ובפ"ב דזבחים (דף יח:): "לא יחגרו ביזע" — שאין חוגרין לא למטה ממתניהם ולא למעלה מאציליהם, אלא כנגד אצילי ידיהם; ואי אצילי היינו אישיל"ש, היאך יחגרו למעלה מהם? ועוד, א"כ, כנגד אציליהן היאך חוגרים? אדרבה, שם היא מקום זיעה! אלא ודאי היינו קוד"א. וכן יש להוכיח מכאן דלא כמפרש דמקום תפילין הוי בקנה למטה ממרפק, דבכל מקום אמרינן: תפילין בזרוע, ובמס' אהלות (פ"א מ"ח) משמע דזרוע הוא למעלה ממרפק. ועוד, דבפ' האומר משקלי (שם ד' יט:) פריך: וביד עד העציל? והכתיב "והיה לאות על ידך", ותנא: זה קיבורית! ומשני: דאורייתא — קיבורית כולה, פירוש: קרויה יד, בנדרים — הלך אחר לשון בני אדם; משמע דמקום תפילין למעלה מן העציל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:5:2.english: With his elbow - This is what is called coude [elbow in Old French], and not as Rashi explained, aisselles [armpits in Old French], since we learned in a Mishnah in Ohalot (1:8): "There are two hundred and forty-eight limbs in a person — thirty in the palm of the hand, six in each finger, two in the forearm [kaneh], two in the elbow [marpek], one in the upper arm [zeroa], two in the shoulder, etc.," which implies that the marpek is below the zeroa. And similarly in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer Mishkali (Arachin 19b): [If someone says,] "My hand or my foot is upon me [to donate its value]," he fills a barrel with water and inserts his hand up to the atzil and his foot up to the knee, and the atzil is called bemarkepo ["his elbow"] in the Mishnah there; and the Targum of "atzilei yadai" (Ezekiel 13:18) is "marpekei yadah," which implies that atzil is coude [the elbow], which is on the arm corresponding to the knee on the leg. And in the second chapter of Zevachim (18b): "They shall not gird themselves with sweat" [Ezekiel 44:18] — meaning they do not gird either below their loins or above their elbows [atzileihem], but rather opposite their elbows [atzilei yedeihem]; and if atzilei meant aisselles [armpits], how could they gird above them? Furthermore, if so, how could they gird opposite their armpits — on the contrary, that is a place of sweat! Rather, it certainly means coude [the elbow]. And likewise one can prove from here against the one who explains that the place for tefillin is on the forearm [kaneh] below the elbow [marpek], for everywhere we say [that] tefillin are [worn] on the upper arm [zeroa], and in Tractate Ohalot (1:8) it is implied that the zeroa is above the marpek. Furthermore, in the chapter HaOmer Mishkali (ibid., 19b), [the Gemara] asks: And on the hand [does one insert it only] up to the atzil? But is it not written, "And it shall be for a sign upon your hand" [Exodus 13:9], and it was taught [in a Baraita]: This [refers to] the bicep [kiboret]! And [the Gemara] answers: With regard to Torah law, the entire bicep — meaning, it is called "hand"; with regard to vows, follow common human parlance. This implies that the place for tefillin is above the atzil.

Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:8:1.hebrew: אישתכח דלמעלה מי' הוה קאי - דמכתף אדם עד לארץ שלש אמות, כדאמר בתרגום מגלת אסתר: פרשנדתא אצטליב על תלת אמין וכן כלהו, וראשיהם היו קטועים. ומקוה דאמר (יומא לא.) דהוי כל גופו עולה בהן אפילו ראש באמה על אמה ברום ג' אמות — דכשיכנס במים יעלו המים למעלה מראשו. וכוכין דאמר בסוף המוכר פירות (ב"ב דף ק.) דאורכן ארבע אמות — היינו עם ראש וצואר ועובי הארון, עם מה שמשקעין ארון בתוך הכוך טפח או טפחיים. וגבי היזק ראיה דהצריך ארבע אמות בריש בבא בתרא (דף ב:) — משום צואר וראש, ובקל יגביה עצמו שיוכל לראות, לכך צריך ארבע אמות. והא דאמרינן במי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מח.) דמקומו של אדם ארבע אמות — היינו כשפושט ידו למעלה מראשו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 92a:8:1.english: It is found that it stood above ten [handbreadths] - for from a person's shoulder to the ground is three cubits, as it says in the Targum to the Scroll of Esther: "Parshandatha was hanged on three cubits," and so all of them, and their heads were severed. And [regarding] a mikveh, where [the Gemara] says (Yoma 31a) that [the volume in which] his entire body can be immersed—even [including his] head—is one cubit by one cubit with a height of three cubits, [that is] because when he enters the water, the water rises above his head. And [regarding] burial niches, where [the Mishnah] says at the end of [chapter] HaMokher Peirot (Bava Batra 100a) that their length is four cubits—that includes the head and neck and the thickness of the coffin, along with the handbreadth or two handbreadths that the coffin is recessed inside the niche. And regarding visual intrusion, where [the Mishnah] required four cubits at the beginning of Bava Batra (2b)—[that is] because of the neck and head, and he can easily raise himself so that he can see; therefore four cubits are required. And that which we say in [chapter] Mi SheHotzi'uhu (Eruvin 48a) that a person's space is four cubits—that is when he stretches his hand above his head.
